text:
mike: FYI — getting a flurry of model timeouts around 10:23 in us-west-2. Traces show requests hitting infra then GPU pods restarting, but I can't find the pod logs in central Loki for the trace IDs. anyone seen this?

sasha: saw gpu_pod_restart alerts at ~10:22-10:25. Also a brief spike in network error logs on nodes. :thinking_face:

jamal: can you paste a trace id so I can correlate in tempo?

mike: trace id: trace-7c9a2f. In Tempo we have full spans for the request and restart, but Loki returns no entries. Query I used:
```
{job="kubernetes-pods"} |= "trace-7c9a2f"
```
no hits.

priya: two quick possibilities: 1) promtail/agent didn't ship logs due to network egress flap, 2) Loki ingestion backpressure dropped incoming batches. Check loki_ingester_append_failed_total and promtail_clients_dropped_lines.

infra-bot: loki_ingester_append_failed_total increased from 0 to 1200 between 10:20-10:26 in cluster-us-west-2 (shard-3).

sasha: that matches. Also noticed large increase in s3_write_latency for object-store which could cause indexer slowdowns.

jamal: try a label-less search across the short window in case labels were stripped:
```
{} |= "trace-7c9a2f" | line_format "{{ . }}"
```
Sometimes when promtail reconnects labels are missing.

mike: ran that too, nothing. I can see the container stdout locally on the node (ssh) but nothing ingested centrally.

priya: can you check promtail logs on that node? promtail usually logs connection/backoff events.

mike: tailing promtail on node gpu-node-07: shows repeated TLS handshake errors and "write tcp: connection reset by peer" around 10:21.

jamal: that points to short egress connectivity issues from nodes -> loki distributor. Any network ACL changes or k8s egress rules recently?

sasha: no infra config changes in the window. But cloud provider reported transient route flaps in us-west-2 between 10:19-10:27 for a subset of AZs. I'll pull VPC flow logs.

infra-bot: VPC flow logs show TCP RST spikes from gpu-node-* to loki-distributor.us-west-2 during 10:20-10:26, matching promtail errors.

priya: that explains missing logs: promtail couldn't push to distributor. Actions: 1) create alert to detect promtail write failures earlier, 2) add short-term buffering for agents, 3) document runbook.

mike: can we backfill? Since the container logs still exist on node, we could run a bulk re-ingest job or ship from node filesystem. Concern about rate limits/tenant quotas.

jamal: for backfill we can run a promtail one-off pointing at archived log files and use a special tenant label so it doesn't blow retention. We should throttle though.

sasha: also check whether indexer shards dropped batches permanently — infra-bot said a nonzero append_failed_total. If those entries were acknowledged by distributor but failed later, we may need to re-run ingest pipeline.

priya: quick PromQL snippets to add to dashboards:
```
sum(rate(loki_client_sent_bytes_total[5m])) by (instance)
sum(rate(loki_ingester_append_failed_total[5m])) by (shard)
promtail_clients_dropped_lines_total
```
Add an error badge when append_failed_total > 0 for 5m.

mike: created a short ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4123 — assigned to jamal. I'll capture the nodes and container timestamps to prepare backfill artifacts.

jamal: assigning oncall to run initial triage: @sasha you're oncall now?

sasha: on it. Starting with VPC flow logs and distributor pod logs. If cloud is the root cause we should file with provider and add a mitigation: increase loki distributor replicas and enable cross-az egress paths.

infra-bot: distributor pod logs (distributor-3) show increased 5xx responses to promtail and flush timeouts at 10:21:22.

priya: while we investigate, recommend temporarily suppressing some noisy SLO alerts tied to missing logs so paging is meaningful. Update: I muted the "log-ingest-errors" alert for 1h.

mike: gathered container log tarball for gpu-node-07 and uploaded to internal bucket s3://redwood-backfill/INF-4123/gpu-node-07.tar.gz

jamal: plan: 1) validate none of the entries exist in Loki (already checked) 2) run promtail backfill with tenant=backfill-<ticket> 3) monitor ingester append metrics and throttle if failures appear. I'll start step 2 in 20m.

sasha: follow-up asks for platform: can we add short-lived local buffering on promtail filesystem to persist lines when egress fails? That would reduce permanent loss for transient flaps. Filing infra improvement ticket.

mike: FYI I also cross-checked Tempo traces for the request span IDs and saved the trace links in the ticket. If backfill successful we should be able to join logs->spans by trace id.

priya: adding retrospective: consider alert that correlates promtail write errors with loki_ingester_append_failed_total and S3 latency. That would catch this earlier.

oncall-bot: @sasha acknowledged INCIDENT-1840123456 — triage started.

sasha: will update ticket with runbook and timelines when backfill completes. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
